traders_and_partners.name: Jock & Trading Partners (incl. Cellmark rep)
traders_and_partners.notes: Provided intel on AD duties (CSC 33-34%, YP 3.2%, PT 10%), oiled GI exemption, Stelco shutdown, Dofasco price hikes, and Dave Stickler's Alberta EAF plan.

cold_rolled_cr.status: Cascadia is CSC's largest CR customer in Canada.
cold_rolled_cr.key_value_proposition: Full size capability ('make every size'), especially light and wide gauges such as 16ga x 60" (1660) and 12ga x 72" (1272), which POSCO refuses to roll when busy.
cold_rolled_cr.primary_end_use: Sold heavily to IEM (Industrial Electric Mfg) for manufacturing house-sized electrical switchboxes for Amazon data centers.
cold_rolled_cr.us_market: Offered to Danny (Cascadia US), though US office needs GI more urgently.

galvanized_and_galvanneal_gi_ga.urgent_inquiry: 10 Gauge (0.13" / ~3.3-3.4mm) x 48" and 60" Galvanneal (GA) and Galvanized (GI). Cascadia will buy at ANY price due to severe Canadian shortage (only ArcelorMittal makes it and puts Cascadia on tight allocation).
galvanized_and_galvanneal_gi_ga.market_shock: Stelco stopped producing GI and CR in Canada, removing 30,000-35,000 MT/month from the domestic market.
galvanized_and_galvanneal_gi_ga.taiwan_bottlenecks: YP (3.2% AD) has no capacity; PT (10% AD) is sold out; CSC has 33-34% 'All Others' AD rate.
galvanized_and_galvanneal_gi_ga.oiled_gi_opportunity: Oiled (unpassivated) GI/GL is excluded from Canadian AD duties; currently used in Ontario for pool walls, evaluated for garage door makers (Flexi-Force, Assa Abloy).

pre_painted_ppgi.status: Will stick with Korea (KG Dongbu), where Cascadia is their largest global customer (70,000 MT/year).

aluminum.status: Imported from China (under company-specific duty remissions) as Canada has no flat-rolled aluminum producer.
aluminum.scrap_arbitrage_story: 6-8 months ago, sold all Chinese secondary aluminum (normally $2.60/lb vs prime $2.75/lb) to US scrap dealers at $2.95/lb, who shipped it duty-free as scrap to Portland to remelt as 'Made in USA'.

stainless_steel.status: Imported partially from Taiwan: YUSCO (燁聯), Tang Eng (唐榮), Walsin Lihwa (華新麗華).

data_centers.overview: Largest and strongest customer segment for Cascadia right now, driven primarily by Amazon.
data_centers.duty_free_channel: US companies manufacture data center modules/equipment in Canada using global steel and copper wire, then ship completed units into the US with zero duty.
data_centers.johnson_controls: Operates 13 plants with 2,000 employees in Edmonton building large cooling fan rooms; buys >3,000 MT/month of sheet/aluminum from Cascadia (account shared with Varsteel for HR/tubing/beams).
data_centers.iem: Builds massive house-sized electrical switchboxes for Amazon data centers using CSC Cold Rolled steel.
data_centers.bottlenecks: Shortage of labor and non-steel components (e.g., cooling fans), causing Amazon to split orders across 3-4 fabricators (all supplied by Cascadia).

north_american_mills.stelco: Owned by Cleveland-Cliffs (US); stopped making GI/CR in Canada; penalizes Cascadia on allocation (3,000 MT/mo HR) and undercuts Cascadia to small end-users by $100/ton.
north_american_mills.arcelormittal_dofasco: Owned by UK/Indian parent; penalizes Cascadia for CITT testimony; sells to Cascadia's customers cheaper than to Cascadia; raised HR by $5 and CR/GI by $10 on Oct 19.
north_american_mills.algoma: Owned by US private equity/hedge fund; supplies 500 MT/mo HR to Cascadia; does not retaliate against Cascadia like Stelco/Dofasco.
north_american_mills.nucor_and_big_river: For next year's contracts, eliminated the previous CRU minus 5.5% discount (now 0% discount) and removed volume buffers; raising prices almost every Monday.
north_american_mills.alberta_new_eaf_project: Dave Stickler (Big River Steel / Hybar founder) is seriously considering building a 500,000 MT/year EAF mill in Alberta.
